title: Displacement prediction sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Reactivity (9F); energy transfer by heating
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 35 (Displacement prediction sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 35: Displacement reactions. To understand how a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound

questions.q: Write the word equation for magnesium + copper sulfate.
questions.a: magnesium + copper sulfate → magnesium sulfate + copper
questions.model: Magnesium is more reactive, so it swaps in: magnesium sulfate. Copper is pushed out as the metal.

questions.q: Will zinc displace iron from iron sulfate?
What colour change shows copper sulfate reacting?
Use the reactivity series to predict six displacements on the sheet; write word equations for those that react.
questions.a: As in the table pattern; for example zinc + iron sulfate → zinc sulfate + iron
questions.model: Teacher does the first prediction aloud with the series.

questions.q: A student's unknown metal X displaces iron but not zinc. Where does X go in the series?
Why is thermite useful for welding railway tracks on site?
questions.a: The reaction is so exothermic it makes molten iron that fills the gap.

questions.q: A more reactive metal ... a less reactive one.
Big question: what happened to the nail in copper sulfate?
questions.a: Iron displaced copper, which coated the nail; iron sulfate formed.
